title: Merge sort the scores
prompt:
Return the exam scores sorted from lowest to highest. Write a merge sort yourself rather than calling the built-in sort: split the list in half, sort each half, then merge the two sorted halves.

- scores has 0 to 100,000 integers between -10^4 and 10^4.
- Repeats are allowed.
- Target O(n log n) time.
hints: A list of 0 or 1 values is already sorted. That is the base case.
To merge two sorted lists, compare their front values and take the smaller one, repeating until one list is empty.
Once one side runs out, append whatever is left of the other.

solution.explanation: Divide: split the list at the middle and sort each half recursively. Combine: two pointers walk the sorted halves, always taking the smaller front value; taking from the left on ties keeps the sort stable. Each level of recursion does O(n) merging work and there are about log n levels.

complexity.notes: The merge needs a buffer of the same size as the input. The recursion is only log n deep, so the call stack is small.

followUps: Write it bottom-up with a loop, merging runs of 1, then 2, then 4.
Merge k sorted lists of scores in O(n log k).
